summary: Not an email provider: deliverability is reputation, not code. This is the mail module that makes the provider replaceable: one interface, an SMTP driver, a hosted-API driver, a dev driver that writes .eml files, DNS records checked, bounces suppressed, and an honest page on self-hosting Postal if you insist.

stack.choice: nodemailer for SMTP, fetch for a hosted API
stack.why: the swap is an env var

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: A sending domain you control DNS for
prerequisites.why: SPF, DKIM and DMARC records are what make mail deliverable.
prerequisites.get: Use a subdomain like mail.yourdomain.com so experiments never hurt your main domain's reputation.
prerequisites.cost: free on a domain you own

prerequisites.name: A hosted provider key (Resend, Postmark or similar)
prerequisites.why: The hosted driver. Free tiers cover thousands of emails a month.
prerequisites.get: Resend: resend.com > API Keys > Create; add and verify your domain. Postmark: account > Servers > API Tokens.

prerequisites.name: SMTP credentials (optional)
prerequisites.why: The SMTP driver, for self-hosting or another provider.

prerequisites.name: Test inboxes at Gmail and Outlook
prerequisites.why: Deliverability is judged by real providers.

env.name: MAIL_FROM
env.where: From address on your verified domain.

env.name: MAIL_DEV_DIR
env.where: Where the dev driver writes .eml files.

phases.title: The interface and two local drivers
phases.goal: send() with a typed result; dev writes files; SMTP sends for real.

steps.do: Define send(to, subject, html, text) returning an id or a typed error; require a text part
commands: mkdir mail && cd mail && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module && npm install nodemailer@6

steps.do: Dev driver writing .eml files; SMTP driver over SMTP_URL

check: Sending in dev writes a file that opens in a mail client
A missing text part fails the send

phases.title: The hosted driver
phases.goal: HTTP with timeout and correct retry rules.

steps.do: Resend driver: POST with a timeout, three retries on 5xx and 429, none on 4xx

check: A rejected address returns a typed error

phases.title: The records
phases.goal: SPF, DKIM, DMARC printed and verified against live DNS.

steps.do: A script that prints the exact records for your domain from the provider's requirements
Check them via DNS and fail loudly on any missing

check: The check passes against live DNS
A real send scores clean on a mail-tester style check

phases.title: Bounces and suppression
phases.goal: Never send again to an address that hard-bounced.

steps.do: A webhook receiver for bounce and complaint events, verified by the provider's signature
A suppression table checked before every send

check: A hard bounce suppresses the address
A later send to it is refused before leaving

phases.title: Self-host option, honestly
phases.goal: A documented Postal path with the warm-up cost stated.

steps.do: Write the docs page on running Postal with reverse DNS and a warm-up plan
Point the SMTP driver at it and send one test

check: The SMTP driver sends through Postal
The README states the warm-up timeline in weeks

phases.title: Operate
phases.goal: Watch bounces and complaints like a provider would.

steps.do: Log every send with provider id and outcome; a daily bounce and complaint rate
Alert when the complaint rate exceeds 0.1 percent

check: A synthetic complaint spike triggers the alert

product.outcome: Email your app can send through any provider, with the reputation work owned by whoever you pay.

operations.incident: A complaint spike: pause sending, find the list source, clean it.

notIncluded: Being a mail provider. Inbox placement is earned with volume history you do not have.
